decisions.reason: A classic lever handle close to the core range costs little to keep listed, and one year on the market is too short for its value to have resolved.
A handle family fits the firm's push toward integrated system families and is cheap to carry while demand from project business is still unfolding.
A new design handle adjacent to established products carries low holding cost and has unresolved market prospects, so the option is still worth keeping.
Like C, this low-cost design variant has no evidence of failure yet, so dropping it would forfeit the option prematurely.
A lever handle family supports system breadth across budget levels and is inexpensive to keep on the market while uncertainty lasts.
The L700 electronic access system with its unique light technology is a strategic option in digital building organization whose high uncertain upside justifies continued commitment.
